evidence.quote: Use your API key SID as the username and your API key secret as the password.
To authenticate requests to the Twilio APIs, use HTTP Basic authentication.
Equivalent to using your Account SID and Auth Token for API requests.
Sign up for a free trial—no credit card required
Start for free. Then pay as you go.
direct, structured access to Twilio's full API surface—over 1,800 endpoints across 30+ products
You can create an API key in the Twilio Console or using the API.

result.notes: Twilio's REST API (Programmable Messaging, Voice, Verify, etc.) uses HTTP Basic auth with either Account SID+Auth Token or API Key SID+Secret (Main/Standard/Restricted key types) — no OAuth2 documented for the core REST API, though Twilio does support OAuth for some newer products (not verified here). Signup is fully self-serve with a no-credit-card free trial that grants trial credit; sending to unverified numbers is restricted until upgrading to a paid account, hence self_serve_trial rather than self_serve_free. Official vendor-hosted MCP server (mcp.twilio.com, docs at twilio.com/docs/ai/mcp) exposes the full API surface (1,800+ endpoints/30+ products) for docs/search; Twilio Labs also publishes a separate alpha local MCP server that can execute API calls. api_breadth marked large based on the 1,800+ endpoint figure from Twilio's own blog (apis.guru's 199-endpoint OpenAPI spec covers only a subset of one product family).
result.one_liner: Twilio is a cloud communications platform providing programmable APIs for SMS, voice, video, email, and messaging channels.
